prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
This 2019 manifesto proposes:

- EU and democracy: Stop Brexit by revoking Article 50 if winning a majority; otherwise back a public vote with an option to remain. Maintain freedom of movement. Extend voting and candidacy rights to long‑term EU residents and implement automatic voter registration and other electoral-law improvements.

- Economy, business, tax and skills: Invest £130bn in infrastructure plus a £50bn regional rebalancing fund; create a Green Investment Bank; expand full‑fibre broadband; support HS2, Crossrail 2 and major rail upgrades; build 300,000 homes a year including 100,000 social. Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; expand Catapult centres; support creative and tech sectors. Introduce £10,000 “Skills Wallets” for adults. Restore Corporation Tax to 20%; replace Business Rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; tax capital gains like income; strengthen anti‑avoidance. Promote responsible business: employee representation on boards, due‑diligence for human rights/environment, binding shareholder pay votes. Support start‑ups, prompt payment, and rights for the self‑employed.

- Work and rights: Create a Worker Protection Enforcement Authority; make flexible working a day‑one right; introduce a “dependent contractor” status with basic protections; curb zero‑hours abuses; strengthen union access.

- Education and childcare: Free, high‑quality childcare (35 hours, 48 weeks) from nine months for working parents and for all two‑ to four‑year‑olds; boost early‑years funding and support. Reverse school cuts, hire 20,000 teachers, fund SEND, modernise buildings. Replace SATs and Ofsted with broader assessment and inspection; protect arts; add a “curriculum for life.” Invest in FE, restore maintenance grants, create a Young People’s Premium, and set mental‑health standards in universities.

- Climate, nature and transport: Net zero by 2045; at least 80% renewable electricity by 2030; ban fracking; a ten‑year home‑insulation programme; zero‑carbon new homes from 2021 (tightening by 2025). Industrial decarbonisation (including CCS), circular‑economy law, ban non‑recyclable single‑use plastics, deposit return schemes. Nature Act, 60m trees/year, habitat and peatland restoration, 50% UK waters as marine protected areas, £5bn flood fund. Clean Air Act, EV‑only new cars by 2030, expand ULEZs, rail electrification by 2035, fares freeze, new Railways Agency.

- Health and social care: Raise £7bn/year via a 1p Income Tax rise for the NHS and social care; £10bn capital upgrade; move toward a dedicated Health & Care Tax; integrate services and pool budgets. National workforce strategy; end GP shortfall by 2025; bursaries for shortage specialties; professionalise care work; stronger carer support. Expand mental‑health access and waiting‑time standards, 24/7 crisis services, perinatal support, and free prescriptions for chronic mental illness.

- Public health and drugs: National Wellbeing Strategy; obesity and food‑labelling measures; tobacco levy; minimum unit pricing for alcohol; legal right to clean air; full PrEP access. Create a regulated cannabis market; divert personal‑possession cases to treatment; shift drugs policy lead to health.

- Welfare, housing and communities: Cut the first Universal Credit payment wait to five days; remove the two‑child limit and benefit cap; raise work allowances; abolish the bedroom tax; raise Local Housing Allowance; end fuel poverty by 2025 via retrofits. Retain the pension triple lock and address women’s state‑pension changes. Build 300k homes/year (100k social), rent‑to‑own, three‑year tenancies, mandatory landlord licensing; end rough sleeping within five years. Invest in rural/coastal services, buses, broadband and mobile coverage.

- Crime and justice: £1bn for community policing; public‑health approach to serious violence; £500m for youth services; Online Crime Agency; end disproportionate stop‑and‑search; stronger support for survivors of abuse; replace Police and Crime Commissioners with Police Boards. Focus prisons on rehabilitation; presumption against short sentences; end prison for possession for personal use; better resettlement support.

- Civil liberties, equality, immigration and asylum: Protect the Human Rights Act and ECHR; restore Legal Aid; end bulk data collection and police facial recognition; modernise family law; reform gender recognition; improve accessibility and tackle period poverty; publish workplace diversity and pay‑gap data; extend paternity leave to six weeks. Overhaul immigration by ending the hostile environment, capping detention at 28 days, creating flexible work/student visa routes, reducing fees, and allowing asylum seekers to work after three months; expand resettlement and family reunion; move asylum policymaking to a development‑focused department.

- Political reform and devolution: Proportional representation (STV), votes at 16, automatic registration, Lords reform, transparency in online political ads and donations, Leveson‑compliant press regulator, citizens’ assemblies. A federal UK with a written constitution and wider devolution to nations and regions.

- Foreign, defence, aid and global climate: Uphold multilateralism; spend 0.7% GNI on aid; lead global climate action; tighten arms‑export controls and suspend sales to rights abusers; adopt Magnitsky‑style sanctions. Require parliamentary approval for military action; meet NATO’s 2% target; strengthen cyber capabilities; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; promote human rights and media freedom worldwide.
